# Vultr: The Infrastructure for Enterprise AI

10 min read October 19, 2026 0

With the promise of AI-enhanced productivity gains and concerns about AI-driven obsolescence, enterprise leaders implementing production AI strategies face tremendous pressure to get things right. Agentic AI deployments offer incredible potential, accomplishing long-term goals with minimal human oversight by leveraging existing tools and processes. Agents automate workflows, scale specialized capabilities, accelerate task completion, and more.

...

- Offers full-stack compute, networking, and storage solutions optimized for agentic AI workloads and more, ensuring the optimal infrastructure is available for both cloud-native and AI-native applications
- Supplies self-service, high-performance GPU and CPU clusters with the flexibility to alter them at will, so enterprises can scale up, scale out, and scale globally without manual requests or configuration delays
- Provides a global presence that enables placing workloads near end users for maximum performance and control over data residency, with data sovereignty options
- Maintains a broad set of compliance and security certifications and attestations as part of a security-first, data privacy-first approach, with advanced identity and access management and security controls 
- Supports an open, composable ecosystem powered by open source technologies, ensuring enterprises can run their preferred choice of AI models and applications without fearing proprietary lock-in
- Delivers a straightforward platform with predictable, transparent, and controllable economics

...

Vultr has a demonstrated track record of more than a decade providing reliable, high-performance infrastructure through a composable, open ecosystem that enables enterprises to deploy their preferred solutions without fear of lock-in. The Vultr cloud platform is a full-stack infrastructure offering with the latest-generation AMD and NVIDIA GPUs, scalable cloud compute powered by the latest data center CPU processors, high-speed networking, powerful storage solutions, managed Kubernetes, managed databases, and more. Self-service CPU and GPU clusters provide enterprises with the flexibility to configure their infrastructure as needed, without waiting for requested changes to be implemented. Vultr’s transparent and predictable pricing empowers enterprises to take control over their cloud costs, while an API-first approach and the simple Vultr Console make Vultr far simpler and more cost-effective to operate than traditional cloud platforms.

...

Simpler self-service CPU and GPU clusters with Vultr Clusters: Enterprises need flexible cloud infrastructure to optimize both agentic AI performance and cost efficiency. Both CPU and GPU clusters are necessary; GPU clusters provide agents with the AI reasoning they need to make decisions, while CPU clusters orchestrate workloads and provide the sandbox space agents need to develop, test, and validate their solutions before taking action. 

Vultr Clusters provides self-service GPU and CPU clusters, which are very simple and easy to provision and use. An upgraded interface in the Vultr Console will soon make it even simpler to provision and modify Vultr Clusters on demand. Automated provisioning ensures enterprise AI infrastructure can be adjusted as needed without wasting high-value compute capacity while waiting for manual configuration.

...

Vultr Cloud GPU instances will also soon have this capability, enabling customers to quickly deploy Vultr’s recent-generation, high-performance virtualized GPU instances from a single validated image, accelerating cluster deployment and reducing time to value for agentic AI deployments. On instances that boot from Vultr Block Storage boot drives, local storage remains available for use as scratch space for AI workloads.

...

High-speed private networking through Vultr Cloud VPNs: The new Vultr Cloud VPN will be available shortly and will provide enterprises with a simple-to-use managed VPN service for connecting their workloads running on Vultr infrastructure to other data centers or client devices over the public internet. This enables enterprises to run their agentic AI operations on Vultr’s infrastructure with low-latency connections to employee workstations and existing applications running on-prem or in other clouds. Vultr Cloud VPNs provide a simple, robust, and affordable way to manage multicloud connectivity architectures. Like with Vultr’s standard egress over the internet, bandwidth will be charged at an extremely affordable $0.01/GB after generous per-instance free allocations are exhausted.

highlights:
# Vultr Announces 34th Cloud Data Center Region in Chennai, India, Among World’s Largest AMD Instinct™ Superclusters

3 min read October 21, 2026 0

India is home to one of the world’s preeminent AI ecosystems. We’re doubling down on our investment in India’s AI future with one of the world’s largest AMD Instinct™ superclusters, deploying in Chennai as Vultr’s 34th global cloud data center region. The supercluster will start at 20 MW of AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs. Further expansion is planned for 2027, featuring next-generation AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs and the AMD Helios™ rackscale solution. The Chennai supercluster meets the moment for an Indian economy with significant AI momentum. AMD Instinct GPUs and the AMD Helios rackscale solution enable enterprises to quickly get AI projects from experimental pilots to large-scale production AI services, with top-tier price-to-performance. And the supercluster aligns with the collaborative, open-source nature of India’s AI landscape: AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD Helios are built on an open software foundation, giving enterprises and developers maximum control and sovereignty over their high-performance workloads. Chennai customers can also access the Vultr Cloud Alliance, featuring strategic pre-built stacks with other tech leaders to enhance composability and support a wide range of industry use cases. We’re writing another chapter in our deep partnership with AMD. With solutions like the AMD EPYC™-powered Vultr VX1™ Cloud Compute, which provides an optimal CPU foundation for agentic AI, as well as our support for the full-stack AMD Helios rackscale solution, together we continue to showcase our joint core belief that openness drives innovation. That belief guides everything we do at Vultr. But beyond just a principle of ours, we believe that it’s where enterprise demand is already moving – which is why our Chennai expansion is just one of many recent and upcoming platform upgrades geared for enterprises worldwide. Enterprises are seeking cloud solutions that deliver the CPU and GPU acceleration, along with full-stack networking and storage solutions, needed to fuel impactful projects like agentic AI – with a rapid path to deployment while maintaining control and flexibility. We see our debut in the Forrester Wave: Public Cloud Platforms, Q3 2026 as a “Strong Performer,” positioning us alongside legacy hyperscalers and above GPU-exclusive neoclouds with shorter track records and greater data privacy concerns, as a sign of that shifting demand. India epitomizes that shift. Now, we’re providing another avenue for enterprises and developers to access infrastructure closer to where they’re building and deploying AI. Get started Sign up to try Vultr and deploy an instance in under 60 seconds. Or, contact our sales team to discuss larger migrations and how Vultr fits into your cloud strategy.

Some workloads need large quantities of compute capacity, fast. Whether it be rapidly scaling infrastructure to support a SaaS application with spiking customer demand, quickly bulking up an E-commerce platform to handle a sudden holiday rush, or other often-changing requirements, flexibility to satisfy demand without the costs of overprovisioning compute or waiting for capacity deployment is essential to make the most of the cloud.

Vultr VX1 plans are designed to power cloud-native workloads economically and efficiently, and they support rapid provisioning at scale. With the option to select Vultr Block Storage boot drives that survive virtual machine deprovisioning, deploying instances is a fast, simple process. Need a lot of compute capacity at once? Vultr VX1 block storage boot drives can be cloned for mass instance creation. Specify the required number of virtual machines and the desired bootable block storage drive, and automation will quickly create the required infrastructure.

## A better model for compute utilization

Traditional cloud infrastructure is often priced around the amount of infrastructure consumed – such as GPU-hours. But in AI research, what ultimately matters is whether a workload is actually completed.

The Grid approaches this differently by pricing around “goodput” – completed, uninterrupted work.

That distinction matters.

A GPU that is technically allocated but sitting idle, waiting on another resource, or interrupted during a workload, is not delivering the same value as infrastructure that consistently keeps a job moving toward completion.

The Grid’s model rewards infrastructure providers that operate reliably, maintain high availability, and engineer systems for efficient utilization. Those are the same principles Vultr applies across its global cloud infrastructure.

results.title: Four critical AI use cases built with GPUs | Vultr Blogs
highlights:
6 min read November 4, 2026 0

...

"For our batch processing and our model training, we can't afford to have a huge cluster of GPUs sitting in our data center. We just don't have the capital for that, so we use a combination of GPUaaS providers ... it's just much more cost-effective for us to rent it for a few hours a week than to own it." – Director, finance & insurance services RegTech, 11-50 employees

This is the GPU-as-a-service use case in its clearest form. The critical infrastructure criterion is cost per GPU-hour — a gap that compounds quickly when GPUs are only needed for a few hours a week. The secondary element is availability: reserved or on-demand access to large clusters without the capital commitment of ownership. For most firms at this scale, renting is not a compromise; it is often the more rational choice.

...

Each of these four use cases points to something different from the underlying infrastructure: compute proximity for computer vision, memory bandwidth for R&D imaging, low cost-per-GPU-hour for batch training and raw cluster density for simulation. Few run efficiently in a traditional general-purpose CPU environment, and most are poorly served by infrastructure designed for a different class of workload.

The leaders we spoke with are building these systems now, often by stitching together offerings from multiple providers because no single platform has fully met all their needs. The common thread: They are looking for the right GPU hardware, close enough to where the work needs to happen, at a cost structure that matches how intermittently or continuously the workloads actually run. However, computing is only part of the equation: The organizations getting real results pair the right infrastructure with clean data, disciplined model training, reliability controls, a clearly defined business outcome and the production processes to sustain performance at scale.
